hooks.text: A three-ton stone lion flew over Beijing’s city walls.
In 1626, a mysterious explosion stripped the clothes off Beijing's citizens.
Why did a massive blast in Beijing strip survivors of their clothes?

title: Why Did a 1626 Explosion Strip Beijing's Citizens? 🤯
description: In 1626, the mysterious Wanggongchang Explosion devastated Beijing, flattening two square kilometers and leaving survivors stripped of their clothes.

beats.text: A three-ton stone lion flew over Beijing’s city walls.
beats.visual: traditional Chinese stone lion guardian sculpture outside

beats.text: In 1626, the imperial Wanggongchang gunpowder armory suddenly exploded.
beats.visual: old map of Peking 17th century showing Beijing walls

beats.text: The blast instantly flattened two square kilometers of the capital.
beats.visual: illustration of historical explosion in a city engraving

beats.text: A mushroom cloud rose, and about 20,000 people perished.
beats.visual: massive mushroom-shaped cloud rising in the distance

beats.text: Strangely, the violent shockwave stripped many victims of their clothes.
beats.visual: painting of the Tianqi Emperor of the Ming Dynasty

beats.text: The Tianqi Emperor fled his breakfast, but his infant heir died.
beats.visual: architecture of the Forbidden City Hall of Union

beats.text: No one ever explained what launched the massive stone guardian.
